data.title: Malibu Boats Launches Response TXi Worlds Preview Ahead of the 2027 IWWF World Waterski Championships
data.description:
LOUDON, Tenn., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Malibu Boats, Inc. , the global leader in performance sport boats, today announced the Malibu Response TXi Worlds Preview, a global series of familiarization events that gives waterskiers the opportunity to get behind the Response TXi with AtmosDrive and experience the boat before competing on it. Running from December 2026 through February 2027, the series stops in Florida, along Australia’s east coast, and at the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships site in Peru.

As the exclusive official towboat partner of the International Waterski & Wakeboard Federation (IWWF), Malibu will tow all IWWF World Waterski Championships with the Response TXi with AtmosDrive, including the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships in Peru (Jan. 10–16, 2027), the 2027 IWWF World Waterski Championships in Australia (Feb. 16–21, 2027), and the 2028 IWWF World Over 35 Waterski Championships (Aug. 27–Sept. 3, 2028). The Worlds Preview gives athletes from every nation the chance to ski behind the boat well before they reach the start dock.

Having pulled 13 world records in waterskiing, the Response TXi is built on Malibu’s T-Cut Diamond Hull, allowing it to track precisely and leave a minimal wake. AtmosDrive delivers more of the engine’s pull into every set: jumpers feel it at the ramp, while slalom and trick skiers feel it through every pass. Many of the world’s top skiers have yet to ski behind the Response TXi, and the Worlds Preview is designed to change that by bringing the boat within reach before competition.

In the United States, the series arrives Dec. 18–20 with a three-day event at Champions Lake in Auburndale, Florida. Athletes from every IWWF member federation can ski timed sets in slalom, trick, and jump, with Will Asher joining Malibu representatives and event staff on the dock throughout the event.

In Australia, Malibu Boats Australia brings the Worlds Preview to four venues across Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland from Dec. 10 through Jan. 22, with priority for Australian Open and U21 team members. Sessions run at Bridgewater, Victoria (Dec. 10–11); Albury, New South Wales (Dec. 18 and 21–22); Marshalls, Queensland (Jan. 14–15), and Stoney Park, New South Wales (Jan. 18–19), with Australian Masters familiarization at Bridgewater on Jan. 22. The same boat will also tow three L-rated tournaments: the Bridgewater Malibu Series, the Albury Jump-Off, and the Australian Masters. For the two weeks before the Worlds, Feb. 1–5 and 8–12, the boat and site at Albury are open to competitors from every nation.

In Peru, two Response TXi boats with AtmosDrive will be at Bujama Lacus, site of the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships (Jan. 10–16, 2027), for official familiarization Jan. 10–12, ahead of preliminary rounds beginning Jan. 13.

Official familiarization and competition will be towed by:

Brand: Malibu

Model: Response TXi

Engine: Monsoon M6Di 430 HP (6.2 Liter)

Transmission: ZF 1.22:1

Speed Control: Zero Off, latest version

Slalom & Trick Prop: OJ 3090 – 4 Blade – 14 × 14

Jump Prop: OJ 3084 – 3 Blade – 14 × 13

“The work that happens before competition matters,” said Rachael Green, General Manager of Malibu Boats. “The TXi is built to give athletes the consistent pull and performance they need to focus on their skiing when it counts. The Worlds Preview gives skiers the chance to experience that performance firsthand and understand what makes the Response TXi a strong competition platform.”

“Confidence in the boat is what lets you push the limits,” added Will Asher, Malibu Pro Team skier. “I worked with our engineers on AtmosDrive so the pull would be something skiers can count on, pass after pass. When you trust the boat, you stop thinking about it and start chasing what’s possible. I’ll be on the dock in Florida to help skiers find that feeling for themselves.”

“The world is coming to Australian water, and the skiers deserve to know this boat long before it counts,” said Noel Gordon, Manufacturing & Process Engineer at Malibu Boats Australia. “From Bridgewater to Stoney Park, our Open and U21 teams will have the chance to log real sets behind the Response TXi all summer. Then, for the final two weeks, we open Albury to skiers from every nation, so when they reach the start dock, the boat already feels like home.”

The Worlds Preview underscores Malibu’s commitment to athlete development and to advancing waterskiing at every level, worldwide. More Malibu Response TXi Worlds Preview events are to come, and Malibu will announce them once they are planned.

About Malibu Boats, Inc.

Malibu Boats, Inc. is a leading designer, manufacturer, and marketer of a diverse range of recreational powerboats, including performance sport, sterndrive, and outboard boats. Malibu Boats, Inc. is the market leader in the performance sport boat category through its Malibu and Axis boat brands, the leader in the 20’–40’ segment of the sterndrive boat category through its Cobalt brand, and in a leading position in the saltwater fishing boat market with its Pursuit and Cobia offshore boats and Pathfinder, Maverick, and Hewes flats and bay boat brands. A leading innovator in the powerboat industry, Malibu Boats, Inc. designs products for a growing range of recreational boaters, fishermen, and watersports enthusiasts who make boating a central part of their active lifestyles. For more information, visit www.malibuboats.com, www.axiswake.com, www.cobaltboats.com, www.pursuitboats.com, or www.maverickboatgroup.com.

data.title: Federal Jury Indicts Russian National on Charges of Spying on Defense Company
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

A federal grand jury has indicted Igor D'iu, a Russian national, on charges he was spying on a U.S. defense-technology firm, according to the Justice Department.

The federal charges allege D'iu conspired to act and acted as an agent of a foreign government without notice to the U.S. Attorney General. He is also charged with interstate stalking and fraud in connection with identification documents, according to the DOJ.

The charges are all related to an alleged scheme to conduct surveillance and gather information about employees of a Silicon Valley technology-defense company, the DOJ said.

D'iu entered the U.S. illegally this summer at the direction of foreign handlers to gather information about the defense company, according to the indictment and affidavit. He received instructions and support from others through the messaging platform Telegram, the documents say.

D'iu wasn't immediately available for comment, and it wasn't clear whether he had legal representation.

The company was allegedly targeted because of its assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia, Craig Missakian, U.S. attorney for the Northern District of California, said.

D'iu had his initial appearance in federal court on Nov. 2 and has remained in federal custody since, the DOJ said. He is set to appear in federal court on Nov. 24, the DOJ added.

If convicted, D'iu faces up to five years in prison for conspiracy and 10 years in prison for acting as a foreign agent, according to the DOJ. He could get up to one year in prison for fraud in connection with identification documents, the agency said. Fines could total as much as $600,000, the DOJ said.

data.title: Copper Settles at Lowest Level Since April Amid AI Market Turmoil, Chinese Demand Concerns — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni and Anthony Harrup

Copper prices tumbled Wednesday to their lowest level in seven months as a stronger U.S. dollar, growing concerns over Chinese industrial demand and a selloff in AI-related stocks overshadowed tightening supplies of the metal.

Three-month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange fell 4.6% to $12,471.00 a metric ton, the lowest settlement since April 7. Front month copper fell 5.3% in New York to $5.6595 a pound, also the lowest since April 7.

The selloff highlights a growing disconnect in the copper market. While inventories in China have fallen sharply and global mine production remains constrained, concerns over the health of the world's second-largest economy are weighing on demand expectations.

China's prolonged property downturn is a particular concern given copper's extensive use in construction, electrical wiring and infrastructure. Although investment in power networks, renewable energy and electric vehicles offers longer-term support, weakness in traditional industrial activity remains a near-term headwind, according to analysts.

Investors have also been unsettled by management turmoil at leading chip maker Nvidia and concerns over tighter regulatory oversight that could slow the expansion of AI infrastructure following the Democratic Party's sweep of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections.

"The recent selloff in artificial intelligence stocks has taken some of the shine off copper, which of course is the metal that actually wires the digital dream together," Price Futures Group senior market analyst Phil Flynn said in a note. "The key question is whether industrial demand actually weakens, or whether the market is simply repricing a crowded growth story."

The weakness in copper spilled across the metals complex, adding pressure on precious metals.

"A firmer dollar and expectations that interest rates may stay higher are weighing on gold and silver, while momentum selling is adding pressure," Flynn added.

Front month gold fell 3.2% in New York to $3,736.80 a troy ounce, its lowest settlement since Sept. 24, 2025. Silver fell 4.8% to $44.999 a troy ounce, also its lowest in almost 14 months.

Minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting supported expectations that the U.S. central bank will raise interest rates in December after a pause last month.

The Fed said almost all participants considered that it would be appropriate to raise rates further, and that a couple of participants said an increase of more than a quarter percentage point "could warrant consideration" at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable.

Higher interest rates would increase borrowing costs for households and businesses, potentially weighing on housing, construction and infrastructure investment--all important sources of copper demand. A stronger dollar could add further pressure by making dollar-denominated commodities more expensive for buyers using other currencies.

Write to Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com and Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Grant of Restricted Stock Units and Warrants to Employees in Genmab
data.description:
Company Announcement

COPENHAGEN, Denmark; November 18, 2026 – Genmab A/S announced today that the Board of Directors decided to grant 4,993 restricted stock units and 4,607 warrants to employees of the Company and the Company's subsidiaries.

Each restricted stock unit is awarded cost-free and provides the owner with a conditional right to receive one share in Genmab A/S of nominally DKK 1. The fair value of each restricted stock unit is equal to the closing market price on the date of grant of one Genmab A/S share, DKK 3,496.

The restricted stock units will vest on the first banking day of the month following a period of three years from the date of grant. Furthermore, the restricted stock units are subject to vesting conditions set out in the restricted stock unit program adopted by the Board of Directors. Information concerning Genmab’s restricted stock unit program can be found on www.genmab.com under Investors > Governance > Compensation > Restricted Stock Units.

The exercise price for each warrant is DKK 3,496. Each warrant is awarded cost-free and entitles the owner to subscribe one share of nominally DKK 1 subject to payment of the exercise price. By application of the Black-Scholes formula, the fair value of each warrant can be calculated as DKK 1,230.13.

The warrants vest three years after the grant date, and all warrants expire at the seventh anniversary of the grant date. The new warrants have been granted on the terms and conditions set out in the warrant program adopted by the Board of Directors on February 23, 2021. Information concerning Genmab’s warrant schemes can be found on www.genmab.com under Investors > Governance > Compensation > Warrants.

Genmab is an international biotechnology company dedicated to improving the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases through innovative antibody medicines. data.title: Wall Street mixed after Nvidia earnings, Fed minutes
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes: Dow down 1.09%, S&P 500 down 0.27%, Nasdaq up 0.34%
  • Fed minutes reveal commitment to hike rates prior to recent round of hot inflation data
  • TJX jumps after forecasting upbeat annual sales
  • Investors await Anthropic IPO pricing

By Stephen Culp and Utkarsh Hathi

US stocks were mixed on Wednesday as investors digested Nvidia results ahead of Anthropic's initial public offering pricing, while weighing hawkish sentiment reflected in US Federal Reserve minutes.

After the three major US stock indexes wavered earlier in the session, by mid-afternoon the Nasdaq turned higher, the Dow was down, while the S&P 500 reversed its modest gains following release of the Fed minutes.

Nvidia's quarterly results released late Tuesday beat analyst expectations, and the AI chipmaker forecast quarterly revenue above estimates. Even so, its shares were down 2.4% amid uncertainties caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden departure last week.

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index , which has handily outperformed the broader market this year, was off 0.7%, underscoring lofty expectations for the sector amid massive spending on AI infrastructure and potential risk associated with the nascent technology.

Anthropic's IPO is expected to price after the market closes on Wednesday. At the top of its $70 to $78 range, the offering would raise about $64.4 billion and value the company at about $1.4 trillion.

Other chipmakers were mixed. Intel was off 1.8%, Micron was down 2%, but Advanced Micro Devices rose 3.2%.

"There's been a lot of dark clouds of uncertainty over technology, chip stocks and AI in general," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha. "It's important to remember the market's not totally falling apart here. It clearly is top-heavy with tech, but there are other groups that are actually doing pretty well under the surface."

Target jumped 6.3% after the discount retailer provided an upbeat holiday outlook. Results from its larger rival Walmart are expected on Thursday.

TJX surged 10.6% after forecasting upbeat annual sales, banking on strong demand ahead of the holiday shopping season.

Take-Two Interactive shares rose 7.7% ahead of the rollout of its Grand Theft Auto VI video game.

On the sector level, consumer discretionary was a clear outperformer, with a boost from a 3.8% gain in Amazon shares.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 555.11 points, or 1.09%, to 50,204.31, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 19.48 points, or 0.27%, to 7,321.05 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 82.36 points, or 0.34%, to 24,410.75.

FOCUS ON THE FED

Minutes from the Fed's October policy meeting showed the central bank remained focused on inflation risks, recognizing the need for further rate hikes if the economy progresses as expected. A few policymakers argued the case for a 50-basis-point rate hike "if incoming inflation data were unfavorable."

Consumer and producer price data released after the October meeting showed hotter-than-expected price growth.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller took a hawkish stance on Wednesday, saying the central bank needs to be more aggressive in responding to inflation. This follows John Williams' comments on Tuesday, in which the New York Fed president said that while he favors tighter monetary policy, there was no need for "dramatic action."

Financial markets are pricing in a 94.7% probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the conclusion of the Fed's December meeting, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Housing data released on Wednesday showed mortgage rates climbing, building permits faltering, and pending home sales dropping to a record low.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.09-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 33 new highs and 551 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 2,345 stocks rose and 2,330 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.01-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 4 new 52-week highs and 8 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 28 new highs and 369 new lows.

data.title: Binance obtains $6.5 billion freezing order from Abu Dhabi court in bid to recover stolen crypto
data.description:
Crypto exchange operator Binance said it has obtained a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts as it seeks to recover crypto stolen in its Oct. 29 hack.

Justice William Stone SBS KC issued the order against unidentified people accused of carrying out the attack, Binance said Wednesday in a statement shared with The Block. The $6.5 billion is the amount covered by the injunction. Binance previously said about $2.85 billion of the roughly $6.34 billion in assets affected by the hack had been frozen or intercepted.

The court also granted interim orders over specific stolen assets and orders requiring assets to be handed over. Some of the interim orders apply to named defendants that have already frozen stolen assets. Binance does not allege wrongdoing by those parties.

Binance said some issuers, exchanges and other partners require a court order before they can release or return funds they have frozen. The orders can be served via blockchain, and the market will be notified as the list of wallets identified as holding stolen funds is updated.

Law firm Gibson Dunn is representing Binance in its efforts to recover crypto assets stolen in the hack. M. Kendall Day of Gibson Dunn called the $6.5 billion injunction "one of, if not the, largest publicly known freezing orders ever made."

"Alongside the worldwide freezing order against the perpetrators, Gibson Dunn has secured proprietary injunctions and delivery up orders on behalf of Binance to recover what was taken. Just as significant is how the orders will work in practice: they can be served via the blockchain, and the market will be notified of a constantly updating ‘living list’ of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets, enabling those assets to be frozen rapidly even as they are laundered at pace," Day said.

Binance said it continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, exchanges and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the stolen funds.

"We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers," said Dugan Bliss, deputy general counsel at Binance.

Tom Robinson, co-founder and chief scientist at blockchain analytics firm Elliptic, previously told The Block that frozen stablecoins could technically be reissued to Binance, but issuers would first want "a clear legal basis," such as a law enforcement request or a court order confirming the rightful owner. He said that process could take weeks or months. At the time, Robinson estimated that about $3.3 billion remained in bitcoin, ether, and XRP, "which no one can freeze."

Robinson also said tools that trace funds across blockchains help investigators flag them to exchanges and issuers faster. "Each time the funds move, there is a chance to catch them," he said.

data.title: Fed Officials Saw Higher Rates Ahead When They Held Steady Last Month — WSJ
data.description:
By Nick Timiraos

Federal Reserve officials thought the economy was likely to require higher rates to bring down inflation when they agreed last month to hold rates steady, and a few officials who supported the decision saw it as a "close call."

Minutes of the Oct. 27-28 meeting, released Wednesday, revealed a cohort of officials — not all of whom may have had a vote at the gathering — thought a rate increase was warranted. "A few of them warned that further delay risked allowing high inflation to become entrenched or necessitating a larger and more disruptive tightening later," the minutes said.

Almost everyone at the meeting thought that, under their most likely scenario for the economy, tighter policy would ultimately be needed, and a few officials warned that inflation might prove more persistent than expected, "in which case a shift to a more restrictive policy stance could become necessary," the minutes said.

Data released since that meeting have tilted the debate in favor of officials who have said the Fed will have to do more to get inflation down. Job growth was solid in October, and underlying inflation was firm for a third straight month. Investors now see a December increase as all but certain, and attention has shifted to how much further the Fed will raise rates next year and how it signals what comes next.

The reverse stock split will become effective at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on November 20, 2026. The Company's common stock will begin trading on a post-split basis at the market open on November 20, 2026, under the Company's existing trading symbol "NIXX", with the new CUSIP number, 75630B501. The reverse stock split is part of the Company's plan to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement of $1.00 per share required to maintain continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market, among other benefits.

The reverse stock split was approved by the Company's board of directors on October 20, 2026, pursuant to Section 78.207 of the Nevada Revised Statutes, and does not require stockholder approval.

The reverse stock split reduces the number of shares of the Company's outstanding common stock from approximately 29.5 million shares to approximately 1.5 million shares, subject to adjustment for the rounding up of fractional shares. As a result of the reverse stock split, proportionate adjustments will be made to the number of shares of the Company's common stock underlying the Company's outstanding equity awards and warrants and the number of shares issuable under the Company's equity incentive plans and other existing agreements, as well as the exercise or conversion price, as applicable. In connection with the reverse stock split, the number of authorized shares of the Company's common stock will be correspondingly reduced from 200,000,000 shares to 10,000,000 shares. There will be no change to the par value per share of the Company's common stock.

Information for NIXX Stockholders

As a result of the reverse stock split, every twenty pre-split shares of common stock outstanding will become one share of common stock. The Company's transfer agent, Nevada Agency and Transfer Company, will serve as the exchange agent for the reverse stock split.

Registered stockholders holding pre-split shares of the Company's common stock electronically in book-entry form are not required to take any action to receive post-split shares. Those stockholders who hold their shares in brokerage accounts or in "street name" will have their positions automatically adjusted to reflect the reverse stock split, subject to each broker's particular processes, and will not be required to take any action in connection with the reverse stock split. Stockholders holding shares of the Company's common stock in certificate form will have their holdings of the Company's common stock automatically adjusted to reflect the reverse stock split.

No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the reverse stock split. Stockholders who otherwise would be entitled to receive a fractional share will instead have such fractional share rounded up to the next whole share.

data.title: Fed Minutes Confirm Most Officials Expect Further Rate Hikes
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - While the Federal Reserve decided to leave interest rates following its October meeting, the minutes of the meeting, released on Wednesday, revealed that the central bank is likely to resume raising rates in the near future.

The Fed minutes said 'almost all participants' judged that further action to raise rates would likely be appropriate in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective.

'A couple of participants noted that an increase of more than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable,' the Fed said.

The central bank also said a few participants observed that inflation could prove more persistent than anticipated, necessitating a shift to a more restrictive policy stance.

Following the October meeting, the Fed announced its widely expected decision to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.75 to 4 percent.

The decision to leave rates unchanged was not unanimous, however, as Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack preferred raising rates by another quarter point following the 25-basis point increase in September.

Nonetheless, most participants expressed support for leaving rates unchanged, with many pointing to the benefits in accumulating additional information.

'These participants cited the need to assess the durability of AI-related investment demand, the evolution of financing conditions, the transmission of the September rate increase to the economy, or geopolitical development,' the Fed said.

The Fed said a couple of participants noted that a gradual approach to policy firming would give businesses and households time to adjust to higher interest rates.

The central bank noted a few participates who supported leaving rates unchanged viewed the decision as a 'close call.'

Meanwhile, the Fed said the participants that favored raising rates by a quarter point emphasized that inflation had remained too high and that they saw few signs of it abating.

'They judged that the current policy stance was not sufficiently restrictive, and a few of them warned that further delay risked allowing high inflation to become entrenched or necessitating a larger and more disruptive tightening later,' the Fed added.

The Fed's next monetary policy meeting is scheduled for December 8-9, with CME Group's FedWatch Tool currently indicating a 94.7 percent chance of a quarter point rate hike.

data.title: Nissan uses Mexico to prep for potential China challenge in US
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nissan exec sees battle vs Chinese in Mexico as 'experiment' for US
  • Nissan cutting costs through simpler engineering, automation
  • The Japanese automaker plans model blitz to revive US business

By Mike Colias

As head of Nissan’s US business, Christian Meunier doesn’t need to imagine what might happen if fast-rising Chinese car brands one day crack the American market. He’s already been confronting that battle south of the border, in Mexico.

Meunier, chairman of Nissan Americas, oversees the Japanese automaker's operations across the Western Hemisphere. He has been fending off an influx of Chinese brands in Mexico, where Nissan has been the top-selling car company for many years.

Meunier said his team is working on reducing costs to be able to match Chinese competitors by shortening the vehicle-development process, reducing supply chain costs and other tactics.

“Our cost base today in [the US] is not competitive. It's not strong enough,” Meunier said at a conference in Detroit hosted by MEMA, The Vehicle Suppliers Association.

REVIVING US BUSINESS A FOCUS

Exports of Chinese cars have surged over the past three years, sending global automakers scrambling to compete with vehicles that often are priced 30% cheaper than domestic models.

For now, Meunier’s main focus is revitalizing the Nissan brand in the US, where the automaker’s market share sank by one-third over a decade through last year. It has been rebounding but, at around 6%, remains well below its peak.

Nissan is planning a blitz of new models to bring back customers. Up first is a hybrid version of its top seller, the Rogue compact SUV, which began arriving at showrooms in recent weeks.

Later in the decade, Nissan plans to roll out several rugged SUVs built on ​a truck-like frame, including the reintroduction of the Xterra, which was sold in ​the US from ⁠the 1990s to the mid-2010s.

For now, Meunier isn't worried about Chinese car brands in the US, where a combination of tariffs and a ban on Chinese software has effectively blocked their entry. But he figures they could show up within the next five or 10 years.

“We need to be ready,” he said at a media briefing Tuesday.

MEXICO AN 'EXPERIMENT' TO PREP FOR CHINESE RIVALS IN US

There is more urgency in Mexico, where Chinese brands have been importing cars to grab a 10% market share in a short period, according to research firm AutoForecast Solutions. A tariff that took effect early this year limits the Chinese companies' ability to undercut the market on price.

Meunier said Nissan has “a two-year window” before the Chinese companies begin making cars in Mexico, avoiding levies. He wants to get Nissan’s costs down during that period through automation and simpler engineering.

He sees that effort in Mexico as a test run for eventually competing against Chinese rivals in the US market.

“Mexico is going to be a really good ground for us to experiment and to learn” how to match the Chinese on cost, he said.

data.title: Epsium Enterprise Limited Reports Unaudited Financial Results for the Six Months Ended June 30, 2026
data.description:
MACAU, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Epsium Enterprise Limited (Nasdaq: EPSM) ("Epsium" or the "Company"), an importer and wholesale distributor of premium alcoholic beverages in Macau, today announced its unaudited financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026.

Revenue for the first half of 2026 decreased to $1.47 million from $3.04 million in the prior-year period amid continued weakness in demand and wholesale pricing for premium Chinese liquor in Macau. Gross profit declined to $0.18 million from $0.50 million. Operating loss increased to $0.75 million from $0.69 million, as lower general and administrative expenses only partially offset the decline in gross profit, while net loss narrowed to $0.67 million from $0.70 million, reflecting higher other income.

First Half 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Revenue decreased 51.8% to $1,466,303 from $3,042,988.
  • Gross profit was $175,353, compared with $495,310; gross margin was 11.96%, compared with 16.28%.
  • General and administrative expenses decreased 22.3% to $918,861 from $1,183,240.
  • Operating loss was $748,194, compared with $691,746. Net loss narrowed 4.5% to $667,598 from $699,106. Net loss attributable to Epsium Enterprise Limited was $667,026, compared with $700,372. Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.05) for each of Class A and Class B ordinary shares in 2026; the 2025 reported loss per Class A ordinary share was $(0.05).
  • Product mix: fine wine accounted for approximately 41% of revenue, compared with approximately 12%; Chinese liquor accounted for approximately 40%, compared with approximately 79%.
  • Balance sheet: as of June 30, 2026, cash was $612,761, inventories, net were $8,255,912 and working capital was $10,579,060, with no bank borrowings.

Management Commentary

"The first half of 2026 remained challenging for premium Chinese liquor in Macau, with continued pressure on both demand and wholesale prices," said Mr. Son I Tam, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Epsium. "We broadened our portfolio toward fine wine and reduced general and administrative costs by more than 20%. Our priorities include converting inventory into cash and exploring new sales channels through Starlight Years."

First Half 2026 Results

Revenue. Sales to gaming and hotel groups decreased approximately 46% to $1,080,050, and sales to the local market decreased approximately 63% to $386,253, as demand for and wholesale prices of premium Chinese liquor remained weak. Sales of Moutai fell to approximately 35% of revenue from approximately 78%.

Gross margin. The decline in gross margin reflected the higher proportion of lower-margin fine wine and continued price competition. Gross margin on sales to gaming and hotel groups narrowed to approximately 15.6% from approximately 22.8%, and local-market sales were realized at approximately breakeven.

Expenses and other income. The decrease in general and administrative expenses reflected lower professional and consultancy fees; the prior-year period included IPO-related costs. Net other income of $82,713 consisted principally of a forgiveness of payable of approximately $78,700 from a supplier on Chinese liquor purchased in a prior period.

Liquidity and Going Concern

Net cash used in operating activities was $1,362,134 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $1,927,422 in the prior-year period. As of June 30, 2026, cash was $612,761, compared with $1,978,728 as of December 31, 2025. Net inventories were $8,255,912, representing approximately 68% of total assets, and working capital was $10,579,060. Although the Company had no bank borrowings, a substantial portion of its current assets consisted of inventories.

The Company does not expect its operations to generate net positive cash flows over the next twelve months. Management has prepared a twelve-month cash flow forecast, based on current trading levels and assuming no new borrowings or equity issuance. Taking into account cash on hand, expected customer collections and management's plans to realize additional cash from existing inventory, management believes substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern has been alleviated. The amount and timing of cash realized from inventory are inherently uncertain. If management's plans do not generate the expected cash, the Company would seek to reduce operating expenditures and inventory purchases and sell inventory through existing channels; there can be no assurance these measures would be sufficient. Investors should review the going-concern discussion, including management's plans, in the Company's Form 6-K.

Recent Developments

Starlight Years Entertainment Limited, 60% owned by the Company's subsidiary Media Icon Limited, completed its commercial registration in Macau during the first half of 2026. The Company intends to use Starlight Years to pursue entertainment and event-promotion opportunities, including beverage sales at event venues.

About Epsium Enterprise Limited

Through its Macau operating entity, Companhia de Comércio Luz Limitada ("Luz"), a limited liability company established under the laws of Macau in 2010, Epsium is engaged in the import and wholesale distribution of primarily alcoholic beverages in Macau. The Company's portfolio includes Chinese liquor, French cognac, Scotch whisky, fine wine, Champagne and other beverage alcohol, sold through gaming and hotel groups, supermarkets, restaurants, bars and other channels across Macau. For more information, please visit epsium.co/investor-relations.

These statements are based on the Company's current expectations and assumptions and involve known and unknown risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied in such statements. Forward-looking statements can be identified by words such as "believes," "expects," "anticipates," "estimates," "intends," "plans," "will," "would," "should," "could," "may," or similar expressions. These statements include, but are not limited to, statements regarding the Company's business strategy, product mix, inventory monetization, management's plans to realize cash from inventory, liquidity and the Company's ability to continue as a going concern, new sales channels and growth initiatives. data.title: Lowe's 3Q Sales Rise, as Professional Customers Drive Growth — Update
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Lowe's reported higher sales in the recent quarter, largely driven by growth in its business selling to professional customers.

Profit climbed as well, thanks to a large tariff refund the home-improvement retailer said it plans to reinvest in the business. Still, Lowe's maintained its earnings outlook for the year and said higher costs are weighing on margins.

Shares fell premarket but pared their losses and were roughly flat in afternoon trading.

Chief Executive Marvin Ellison on Wednesday said professional customers are responding well to enhancements Lowe's has made to its fulfillment network. At the same time, loyalty offerings are helping the company to deepen customer relationships and capture more spend.

Third-quarter net sales climbed 9.3% to $22.76 billion, just ahead of Wall Street estimates for $22.39 billion. Growth across Lowe's professional business--as well as its home-services unit and online sales channels--helped offset softer trends across the company's do-it-yourself business.

There are some green shoots, though. For instance, Lowe's logged its strongest quarter of appliance sales in five years, Ellison said on a call with analysts.

"That says a lot when you think about the pressure that the DIY consumer is under," he added.

Lowe's results echo those of rival Home Depot, which also reported higher sales and profit in the latest quarter, helped by strength among professional contractors despite continued weakness in the broader home-improvement market.

Lowe's said comparable sales, which account for store openings and closings, climbed 1.8% for the three months ended Oct. 30, ahead of analyst views for a 0.1% gain. Higher average tickets, which in part reflected inflation in commodity-driven categories such as lumber and electrical cable, offset a decline in comparable transactions, Chief Financial Officer Brandon Sink said.

For the year, Lowe's now expects same-store sales to tick up 0.5%, whereas they were previously expected to be flat.

Profit climbed to $1.67 billion, from $1.62 billion a year earlier. Adjusted earnings came in at $3.10 a share, including a 34-cent benefit tied to tariff refunds. Analysts were looking for adjusted earnings of $2.88 a share.

Excluding the tariff refund, Lowe's said its bottom line was pressured by recent acquisitions, as well as elevated fuel and transportation costs. Productivity initiatives spanning merchandising, stores, supply chain and corporate functions are helping to offset that pressure, Sink said.

Lowe's reinvested about a third of its $250 million tariff refund back into the business during the third quarter, and the company expects to reinvest the remainder during the fourth.

"Our intention is to reinvest our tariff refunds in ways that strengthen our customer value proposition by putting these dollars to work to enhance the customer experience, strengthen our competitive position, and bring value to our customers," Ellison said.

For the year, Lowe's continues to expect earnings of about $11.25 a share, or about $12.25 a share on an adjusted basis.

Comstock announced in September a $1.65B strategic partnership with Azerbaijan's SOCAR in exchange for non-operating working interests in its legacy and Western Haynesville assets; concurrently, Comstock majority owner Jerry Jones entered into a joint venture to fund the drilling and completion costs of some legacy and Western Haynesville wells in exchange for an ownership stake.

Morgan Stanley analyst Devin McDermott said while he views the transactions positively, as they improve Comstock's liquidity position, he still forecasts an outspend in 2027 at $3 Henry Hub.
